instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Secure the Endorsement
cards.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to project. Now endorse my new rota into this microphone so the whole staff meeting hears you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already told you it was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, privately. You're still saving your strong voice for ordering lunch. Tell the people who might object.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I email instead? I'd rather put the reasons in writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to prepare. Copy the whole staff and sign it. Then when they challenge the rota, I can read your reasons back to them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign here to support my kitchen extension. I taught you to trust your judgment; let's put it where the neighbours can see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the plans, but I'd rather not put my name down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still hiding the good answer. How can I tell them the people next door approve if you won't say who you are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I use initials?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A start. Print your full name underneath, like I showed you on forms. Then no one can say I've invented my supportive neighbour.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sink's blocked. You're still my junior coordinator; call the plumber. I taught you how to handle these little emergencies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran yesterday's whole event. You promised me a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And my training clearly paid off. Senior coordinator, then. Still reporting to me, but you can supervise the plumber.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can lock up too. Look at that: your first senior responsibility. Remember the alarm code I drilled into you; I won't stay to remind you.

beats.text: You can answer the inspector's complaints. I taught you to write those replies; that's what a deputy is for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're mostly about your decisions.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign 'Deputy,' then. You're ready to answer questions without me beside you. Just don't promote yourself when you introduce yourself.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I book the trip, tell me who can still cancel it. Remember the approval checks I taught you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've found the yes. Good. Now who could stop the deposit? I taught you to check the no as well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer. But she's away; her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. You've found the person at the keyboard. Does she decide, or does she still need the treasurer's permission? Don't confuse those again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The pipe's still leaking. Show me you've remembered my lesson: whose signature actually releases the repair money?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got all three. It took the whole morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neat work. But I taught you to follow the money, not collect autographs. Who could still freeze it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance. They unfroze the roof payment when the caretaker called, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're getting somewhere. Could the caretaker overrule them, or did he ring someone who could? Find that out before you spend another morning on signatures.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me for the shed vote. I taught you to speak up for this allotment; don't leave me looking like the only person who wants it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll support it if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally thinking about the whole site. Everyone gets a key. Come and make that case beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them over. Explain the shared-key promise, like I taught you. Then ask them to join us; a row of supporters will say more than your teacher and an empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add your name to my request for late pottery-room hours. I taught you to make a case; help me make this one look less lonely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I leave at five. It won't help me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still arguing only your own corner. Your name would show the evening class isn't asking for special treatment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The morning class wants weekend access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're looking past your own timetable. Add weekends and bring two of them. You can explain why several classes need better access; I'll stand beside you if you lose your place.
